title: Multimodal speech processing in static and dynamic cocktail-party situations
summary: In everyday life, speech is perceived both through the ear and through the eye. The latter is typically referred to as ‘lip-reading’. People with hearing impairments often use lip-reading, particularly in difficult situations where several people are speaking at the same time. The extent to which this is used for speech recognition, as well as the underlying mechanisms, have not yet been fully investigated. The study aims to provide relevant information that can be used to improve hearing diagnostics and rehabilitation.

interventions.name: Individuals with cochlear implants. Assessment of speech recognition and cognitive load using pupillometry, and of attention using eye-tracking. Tests of basic cognitive abilities such as working memory and attention. Four appointments.
Individuals with age-appropriate hearing as "control group".

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Individuals fitted with cochlear implants. Subjects with age-appropriate hearing as a ‘control group’. Normal or corrected-to-normal vision. As speech tests will be carried out, a very good command of German is required.
Exclusion criteria:
Insufficient command of German, poor speech recognition, visual impairments, known cognitive limitations
